newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Marcopper says Philippine mine spill "act of God".
newsitem.headline: Marcopper says Philippine mine spill "act of God".

text.p: Lawyers for Marcopper Mining Corp said on Thursday a spill of waste from its copper mill was "an act of God" and asked a Philippine court to dismiss criminal charges against three of the company's top executives.
The lawyers submitted their petition in a court session in which charges against the three were to be read.

Reading of the charges, however, was postponed indefinitely until the petition for dismissal was resolved, court clerk Eduardo Miciano told Reuters by telephone in the central Philippine town of Boac.
The three Marcopper officials are chief executive officer and president John Loney, resident manager Steven Reid, both Australians, and their senior manager Pedro Hernandez.
The three had been charged with violations of the Philippine Mining Act, the Water Code and the Pollution Control Law, as well as reckless imprudence resulting in damage to property.
Marcopper's ore mill in Marinduque, 160 km (100 miles) south of Manila, has been closed since March when waste from its Tapian storage reservoir swamped a 25-km (15-mile) long river.

Marcopper lawyers said Loney and Reid should not be held liable for the "accident" since they were not connected with the company when the Tapian pit was constructed in 1975 and after the government approved the use of the pit as the mine's waste reservoir in 1990.

Loney and Reid, both nominees of Canada's Placer Dome Inc which owns 40 percent of the mine, have since resigned from Marcopper. Placer said they had resigned because the company had withdrawn its interest in the mine.

The spill of mine tailings into the Boac, Makulapnit and Boac rivers occurred after an earthquake measuring 3.21 on the Richter scale in March created fractures in the waste reservoir, Marcopper said.
"It need not be stressed that no one can be held liable for an act of God," Marcopper said.
